title: Chapter 4: Marginalized, Minorities, and Vulnerable Groups
content: ሰላም! 🖐️ እንኳን ወደ Social Anthropology (ምዕራፍ 4 - ክፍል 1) በደህና መጡ! በዛሬው ክላሳችን 4.1 እና 4.2 እናጠናለን ተከታተሉኝ👇📚💡 --- Unit Overview & Introduction * Unit Four focuses on issues of marginalization and vulnerability, specifically dealing with different forms of marginalization affecting the rights and wellbeing of minority occupational groups, women, children, older people, religious, and ethnic minorities. * It discusses the human rights approaches and the notion of inclusiveness. * Students are expected to take an active role in class activities, group work, and individual learning activities to build independent analytical skills. 👉 ይህ ክፍል ትኩረት የሚያደርገው በማህበረሰቡ ውስጥ በልዩ ልዩ ምክንያቶች የተገለሉ (Marginalized)፣ ቁጥራቸው አነስተኛ የሆኑ (Minorities) እና ለጉዳት የተጋለጡ (Vulnerable Groups) የህብረተሰብ ክፍሎች ላይ ነው። ይህም የሴቶች፣ የሕፃናት፣ የአረጋውያን፣ የሙያ አነስተኛ ስብስቦች (Occupational Groups)፣ የሃይማኖትና የብሔር አነስተኛ ስብስቦችን መብትና ደህንነት ያጠቃልላል። 💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ የዚህ ክፍል ዋና አላማ የመገለልና የተጋላጭነት መንስኤዎችን በጥልቀት መረዳት ነው! --- 4.1 Definition of Concepts 1. What is Marginalization? * Marginalization is defined as the treatment of a person or social group as minor, insignificant, or peripheral. * It involves the exclusion of certain groups from social interactions such as marriage relations, sharing food and drinks, and working or living together. * Example in Ethiopia: Minority occupational groups (e.g., potters and tanners) are not allowed to be members of community-based associations like Iddirs in some regions. * Marginalization excludes certain groups from basic economic rights, including rights to property ownership and rights to engage in certain economic activities or jobs. 👉 Marginalization (ማግለል/ከዳር ማቆም) ማለት አንድን ግለሰብ ወይም የማህበረሰብ ክፍል አነስተኛ፣ ዋጋ የሌለው ወይም ከዋናው ማህበረሰብ የተገለለ (peripheral) አድርጎ መመልከትና ማግለል ነው። ይህም ከማህበራዊ ግንኙነቶች (እንደ ጋብቻ፣ አብሮ መብላትና መጠጣት፣ አብሮ መኖር) እና ከኢኮኖሚ መብቶች (መሬትና ንብረት ማራት) ማግለልን ያጠቃልላል። 💡 Exam Hint: በፈተና ላይ የዕድር (Iddir) አባልነት ክልከላ የትኛው መገለል እንደሆነ ከተጠየቃችሁ መልሱ Social Exclusion/Marginalization ነው! 2. Who are Mostly Marginalized? * Targets of marginalization vary from society to society due to cultural diversity. * Commonly marginalized groups across the world include: * Women and Girls * Children * Older People * People with Disabilities (PWDs) * Religious, Ethnic, and Racial Minorities * Minority Occupational Groups (e.g., tanners, potters, and ironsmiths in Ethiopia). 👉 በብዛት መገለል የሚደርስባቸው ማህበረሰቦች፦ በዓለም ዙሪያና በኢትዮጵያ ሴቶች፣ ህፃናት፣ አረጋውያን፣ አካል ጉዳተኞች፣ አነስተኛ የሃይማኖትና የብሔር ስብስቦች እና የእጅ ጥበብ ባለሙያዎች (ሸክላ ሠሪዎች፣ ቆዳ ፋቂዎች፣ ብረት ሠሪዎች) የመገለል ሰለባ ይሆናሉ። 3. What is Vulnerability? * Vulnerability refers to the state of being exposed to physical or emotional injuries, attacks, harms, or mistreatment. * Impacts are not limited to physical damage; they lead to long-term issues including emotional disorders (e.g., psychological trauma) and social or relational problems. * Examples of Vulnerability: * Girls and women are vulnerable to gender-based violence (harassment, rape, forced marriage). * Young girls are exposed to child/early marriage (before age 15) in parts of Ethiopia, leading to teenage pregnancy, severe reproductive health problems such as fistula, and social isolation. * Vulnerable groups require special protection, attention, and support (e.g., protecting children from FGM/C, special education programs introduced in universities for students with disabilities). 👉 Vulnerability (ተጋላጭነት) ማለት ለአካላዊ ወይም ሥነ-ልቦናዊ ጉዳት፣ ጥቃትና የበደል ድርጊት የተጋለጠ መሆን ነው። ለምሳሌ፦ ሴት ልጆች ለአካላዊና ጾታዊ ጥቃት፣ ለአስገዳጅ/ያለ ዕድሜ ጋብቻ እና ለፊስቱላ (fistula) በሽታ ተጋላጭ ይሆናሉ። 💡 Exam Hint: "The state of being exposed to physical/emotional injuries" ከተባለ መልሱ Vulnerability ነው! 4. Minority Groups * Refers to a small group of people within a community, region, or country that differs from the majority population in terms of race, religion, ethnicity, or language. * Examples: Blacks in the USA (racial minority), Christians in a Muslim-majority country, or Muslims in a predominantly Christian society. 👉 Minority Groups (አነስተኛ ስብስቦች) ማለት በቁጥር አነስተኛ ሆነው በዘር፣ በሃይማኖት፣ በብሔር ወይም በቋንቋ ከብዙሃኑ የሚለዩ ስብስቦች ናቸው። --- 4.2 Gender-based Marginalization Sex and Gender Distinction * Sex: Refers to biological differences between females and males, genetically expressed through chromosomes, hormones, and physiological traits. * Primary differences: Sexual and reproductive organs (e.g., only women can get pregnant, give birth, and nurture newborns). * Secondary differences: Breasts, voice pitch, and hair distribution pattern. * Other variations: Differences in height, weight, and physical strength (men tend to be taller, heavier, and stronger - Kottak 2005). * Gender: Refers to socially and culturally constructed characteristics, roles, and behaviors assigned to men and women. * Gender Roles: Tasks assigned by culture (e.g., men as leaders/assertive/outdoors; women as caring/nurturing/indoor home management). * Gender Stereotypes: Strongly held views about characteristics of males and females. * Gender Inequality: Discrimination based on gender, arising from cultural values, norms, and beliefs rather than biological differences. 👉 Sex vs Gender (ባዮሎጂካል ጾታ እና ማህበራዊ ጾታ)፦ * Sex (ተፈጥሯዊ/ባዮሎጂካል ጾታ)፦ በክሮሞሶም፣ ሆርሞንና ተፈጥሯዊ አካል የሚለይ (ለምሳሌ፦ መፀንስና መውለድ)። * Gender (ማህበራዊ ጾታ)፦ ህብረተሰቡ የሰጠው ሚና፣ ባህሪና አስተሳሰብ ነው። 💡 Exam Hint: Sex ተፈጥሯዊ (Biological) ሲሆን፣ Gender ግን በማህበረሰብ የተገነባ (Socially constructed) ነው! በፈተና እንዳትሸወዱ! 🎯 --- Harmful Traditional Practices (HTPs) & FGM/C Female Genital Mutilation/Cutting (FGM/C) * FGM/C is a form of gender-based violence and a major Harmful Traditional Practice (HTP). * Over 200 million women/girls alive today have undergone FGM/C, and over 3 million are at risk annually in 28 African countries (Shell-Duncan et al., 2016). * Global Prevalence: Highest in Somalia (98%), Djibouti (93%), Egypt & Sudan (87%), and Eritrea (83%). Lowest in Nigeria (25%), Senegal (24%), and Kenya (21%). FGM/C Prevalence in Ethiopia (CSA & ICF 2016 Data) * Around 65% of girls and women aged 15–49 are circumcised in Ethiopia (declined from 80% in 2005). * Regional Breakdown (High to Low): * Somali: 99% * Afar: 91% * Harari: 82% * Oromia: 76% * Dire Dawa: 75% * Benishangul-Gumuz: 63% * Amhara: 62% * SNNP: 62% * Addis Ababa: 54% * Gambela: 33% * Tigray: 24% * Age Differences: Performed shortly after birth in Amhara, Tigray, Afar, and Northern Oromia. Performed as a rite of passage approaching marriage in Southern Ethiopia. 👉 በኢትዮጵያ የ FGM/C ስርጭት (65%)፦ በሶማሌ (99%) እና አፋር (91%) ከፍተኛ ሲሆን፣ በትግራይ (24%) እና ጋምቤላ (33%) አነስተኛው ነው። 💡 Exam Hint: የክልሎችን የፐርሰንቴጅ ደረጃዎች በደንብ ያዙ! 📊 --- Key Drivers / Cultural Causes of FGM/C 1. Belief in Impurity: Uncut women are considered impure and believed to bring misfortunes (illness, infertility, crop failure, wealth loss) upon their husbands. 2. Discouraging Promiscuity: Belief that uncut girls have extraordinary sexual desire and would be promiscuous/unfaithful, leading to divorce. 3. Preserving Virginity: Very strong value attached to premarital virginity (e.g., Type III FGM/C / infibulation). 4. Fear of Ill-manner: Belief that uncut girls will be disobedient, powerful, and ill-mannered. 5. Social Sanctions: Families undergo FGM/C due to fear of isolation, ridicule, insults, and inability to find a husband for their daughter. Negative Impacts of FGM/C * Severe bleeding, infections, severe pain during sexual intercourse, childbirth complications, psychological trauma, and long-term emotional disorders. 👉 የ FGM/C ዋና ዋና ምክንያቶችና ጉዳቶች፦ * የእርኩሰት እምነት (Impurity): ያልተገረዘች ሴት ዕድል ቢስነትን ታመጣለች የሚል የተሳሳተ እምነት። * ሴሰኝነትን መቀነስ (Discouraging Promiscuity) እና ድንግልናን መጠበቅ (Preserving Virginity)። * ማህበራዊ ማግለልን መፍራት (Social Sanctions)። 💡 Exam Hint: እነዚህ አምስቱ ነጥቦች FGM/C እንዲቀጥል የሚያደርጉ ዋና ዋና Cultural Drivers ናቸው! --- ለዛሬ ከዚህ ላይ ይበቃናል። በቀጣይ PART 2 እንቀጥላለን! 🌟 መልካም ጊዜ!
